learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for drafting, signing, and developing projects in the mechanical technological field of industrial engineering, whose objective is, in accordance with the acquired knowledge as established in section 5 of this order, the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Capacity for directing the activities object of the engineering projects described in the previous paragraph.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Capacity to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Capacity for handling mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Capacity to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and capacity to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Capacity to apply quality principles and methods.
Knowledge and capacities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Is able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.
Analyze and solve static and hyperstatic beams, frames, arches, and rings subjected to external loads, taking into account the principles of material resistance.
Calculate and analyze the deformation of columns subjected to buckling.
Know and apply the Theory of Elasticity to the behavior of elastic solids and real solids.
Is able to perform experimental tests in the laboratory using experimental methods for stress and strain analysis.

syllabus_topics: Constitutive equations of elastic solids: Elastic anisotropy
Experimental methods for stress and strain analysis (Extensometry and Photoelasticity)
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, two partial controls (45% each) and problem-solving (10%) are used. To pass, no partial control score can be below 5. For those who do not pass by continuous assessment, a final exam will evaluate the unpassed parts (90% of the final grade, 45% for Part 1 and 45% for Part 2), with the remaining 10% from problem-solving. Students who do not pass in the ordinary exam will take a final exam covering the entire syllabus, with a weight of 100% of the final grade.
